title: City-Wide Asset Governance, Operator Assurance, and Phased Vesting: A Qiddiya Case Study
content: How can an asset owner preserve service, accountability, and lifecycle value when infrastructure crossesorganizational boundaries and changes operator? This conceptual case study develops an owner-led frameworkusing Qiddiya as its public context. Six service domains are connected through common evidence, acceptance,and interface controls. A four-ledger model separates legal title, custody, operating duty, and financial recognition.The analysis compares centralized, operator-led, and federated governance; works through service-credit andcooling-investment calculations; and examines three hypothetical crises. The preferred federated design isconditional on competent domain owners and enforceable interfaces. Public sources establish context; operatingcases, budgets, and thresholds are assumptions. Arithmetic and scenario consistency do not establish operationaleffectiveness. A bounded pilot is proposed to test whether the design improves decision traceability withoutexcessive approval burden.
